name: Hexagonal BN (Pease AA-prime structure, 35°C)
citation: R. W. G. Wyckoff (1963). Crystal Structures, second edition, vol. 1, pp. 85–237 (direct COD/AMCSD compilation source). Experimental cross-check: R. S. Pease (1952). An X-ray study of boron nitride. Acta Crystallographica 5, 356–361. DOI: 10.1107/S0365110X52001064.
conditions_evidence: Pease1952 p357 reports the identical a=2.50399±0.00005, c=6.6612±0.0005 Å lattice at 35°C, with camera temperature 35±0.5°C. The raw COD compilation does not itself give temperature. Numeric pressure of this cell determination is not specified; the vacuum condition of the separate high-temperature expansion experiment is not transferred.
method: Experimental Cu/Mn powder X-ray diffraction in Pease1952; raw COD/AMCSD structure is the later Wyckoff1963 compilation. Cell and ordered AA-prime stacking were checked against the original paper; this is not a DFT structure.
synthesis_conditions_note: Pease1952 p357: commercial B.D.H. material recrystallized at 2050°C for about two hours in flowing nitrogen. This is synthesis/recrystallization, not diffraction temperature.
selection: The unmodified COD compilation agrees with the experimentally established Pease cell and AA-prime B-over-N stacking; select both species' single independent sites and full three-neighbor first shells.
notes: The raw CIF directly cites Wyckoff1963, not Pease1952. The provenance explicitly retains both identities; Pease DOI is an experimentally checked supporting citation, not an invented DOI in the raw COD file.

Pease reports stacking faults and traces of impurities (<0.6 wt%). The periodic ordered model encodes the average AA-prime structure and does not simulate those faults, impurity sites or thermal layer puckering.
Do not substitute the previously proposed graphite-like stacking rejected by Pease. The parsed full unit cell has two B and two N atoms with no partial site occupancy.
BN is anisotropic. These paths do not establish polarization-dependent XANES accuracy, and a single first-shell path does not represent multiple-scattering or interlayer physics.

Low-energy light-element K-edge FEFF paths are unvalidated candidate scattering references, not a demonstration of usable measured EXAFS or XANES accuracy. Core excitons, band structure, charge transfer and nonspherical potentials can matter near these edges; retain actual SCF convergence, potential and executable diagnostics.

A nominal native k grid is not an experimental usable k range. Choose an absorber/edge-appropriate measured range and validate against data; a converged FEFF calculation alone does not validate this reference.
The source specimen contains observed stacking faults. This ordered periodic reference does not model faults; applicability to turbostratic, rhombohedral or other BN phases is unvalidated.

experimental_cross_check.evidence_location: pp357–358 cell, diffraction temperatures and selected structure B; p360 first-neighbor bonding and layer stacking.
experimental_cross_check.stacking: AA-prime: B directly over N between successive layers
experimental_cross_check.correspondence: The original-CIF cell values exactly match the original experimental values. Its P63/mmc B2c/N2d coordinates expand to an alternating B/N four-atom AA-prime cell, with first-neighbor distance a/sqrt(3). No cell adjustment or element substitution was performed.
experimental_cross_check.read_limitation: Verified original article text through indexed scan; direct publisher full PDF requires access. No full journal PDF is included.
